unit.title: HTML: the page skeleton
unit.description: DOCTYPE, html, head and body, title, comments, bold and italic, div and span

cards.definition: The first line of every page; it tells the browser to use modern HTML rules.
cards.example: Without it, browsers fall back to an old, quirky display mode.

cards.definition: The two parts of a page: the first holds information about the page (title, styles), the second everything displayed.
cards.example: The text of the page goes in body, never in head.

cards.definition: A note between <!-- and --> that the browser does not display.
cards.example: <!-- Main menu --> above a menu says what follows.

cards.definition: Mark important text (shown in bold) and stressed text (shown in italics).
Generic containers with no meaning of their own: the first is a block, the second sits inside a line of text.
cards.example: <div class="card"> groups a product; <span class="price"> marks a price in a sentence.

cards.definition: Forces the text to continue on the next line, inside the same paragraph.

exercises.prompt: Which line comes first in an HTML page?
exercises.explain: The page starts with <!DOCTYPE html>, then <html>, which contains <head> and <body>.
whyWrong: <html> comes right after the DOCTYPE line.

exercises.prompt: Put the skeleton of a page in order, from top to bottom.
exercises.explain: DOCTYPE first, then html, which holds head (information about the page) then body (what is displayed).

exercises.prompt: Where does the text of the page go?
exercises.explain: Everything people see on the page goes in body. head only holds information about the page.
whyWrong: head holds information about the page, not what is displayed.
title is only the name in the browser tab.
Nothing should come after the closing </html>.

exercises.prompt: Where does the text inside <title> appear?
choices: At the top of the page, in big letters
At the bottom of the page
exercises.explain: title gives the name of the page: it shows in the browser tab and in search results. The big visible title is an <h1>.
whyWrong: The big visible title is an <h1>, inside body.
title is never displayed inside the page.
It is shown in the tab and in search results.

exercises.prompt: What does the browser display for the first line?
exercises.explain: Everything between <!-- and --> is a comment: a note for developers, never displayed.
whyWrong: Comments are never shown on the page.
Comments are valid HTML, so there is no error.
A comment adds nothing to the page.

exercises.prompt: Which tag marks important text, shown in bold by default?
exercises.explain: strong means important (bold by default); em means stressed (italic by default).
whyWrong: em is for stressed text, shown in italics.
<big> is an obsolete tag; use CSS for size.

exercises.prompt: A <span> starts on a new line, like a paragraph.
exercises.explain: span is inline: it stays inside the line of text. div is the block container that starts on a new line.

exercises.prompt: How does the browser display this address?
choices: On two lines: Main street, then Paris
On one line: Main street Paris
exercises.explain: forces a line break inside the same paragraph. It is an empty element: no closing tag.
whyWrong: breaks the line, so Paris goes to the next line.
The tag is read by the browser, not displayed.
It is still one paragraph, split over two lines.

exercises.prompt: Build the title shown in the browser tab: My shop.
exercises.explain: <title>My shop</title> goes in <head>; it names the page in the tab.

exercises.prompt: The heading Welcome does not appear on the page. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain:
Visible content belongs in body, not head. Move

Welcome

into .

exercises.prompt: Build a sentence where only the word sale is important (bold).
exercises.explain:
Big sale

: strong marks the important word inside the paragraph.
